notes: v5 is the first re-anchoring since v3, and the first to be measured on a corpus that contains games schema 3 made expressible. Four changes, in descending order of how much they move a score.  (1) THE ROSTER IS WIDER. Six minimax budgets (100/200/400/800/1600/6400) rather than four, at 4 games per ordered pairing, seed 0. `gradient_persistence` compares the slope of the lower half of the ladder against the upper half, and with four budgets the two halves shared a point; with six they do not. That is what removes knightmate's spurious zero, and it is a roster problem rather than a component problem. It also breaks up the deterministic sweeps that made a Bradley-Terry interval look confident while containing no information.  (2) THREE COMPONENTS ARRIVE FROM STAGE 12, on the evidence in docs/reference/stage-12-measurements.md and not before it. `progress_irreversibility` (spread-to-noise 29.1) is the share of plies that could never be undone -- the irreversible process a designer named as the cure for repetitiveness -- scored as a BAND, because the two worst games in the corpus measure 1.000 and a game where every ply is irreversible is over in a handful of moves. `instance_participation` (18.7) is the share of pieces that ever moved, which is the axis `piece_utilisation` averages away; it does NOT rescue `piece_utilisation` from `mutant-instant-promotion` and was never adopted on that promise. `lead_conversion` (3.6) is the weakest-measured of the three and the most independent -- maximum correlation +0.41 against anything already scored -- which is why it is in at all: a modestly measured signal nothing else carries beats a precisely measured restatement.  (3) TWO EXISTING WEIGHTS COME DOWN, because the new components measured against them. `progress_irreversibility` correlates -0.80 with `blunder_recoverability` on raw values, and `instance_participation` +0.72 with `distinct_game_rate` while covering ground `piece_utilisation` claims. Both of those correlations are real overlap rather than saturation, so `blunder_recoverability` goes 0.08 -> 0.05 and `piece_utilisation` 0.06 -> 0.04. Wanting both halves of a correlated pair is allowed; paying full weight for both is double-counting.  (4) `capture_availability` IS REJECTED and `position_revisit_rate` and `threat_asymmetry` ARE HELD, all three on measurement rather than taste. `capture_availability` is the best-measured candidate of the seven at 51.7 and correlates -0.84 with `piece_utilisation`; `position_revisit_rate` has a corpus spread narrower than the curve span the anchoring floors require, so a compliant curve would be flat across every real game; `threat_asymmetry` is the one whose value should rise after schema 3 gives it a capture matrix to read, and it is re-read then rather than guessed at now. `traversal_time` is a diagnostic and a candidate grid axis and is never scored.  WHAT DID NOT CHANGE. The judge still contributes nothing: `llm_weight` stays 0.0, and the pairwise ordering is still a tie-break rather than a term. The gates are unchanged except where the roster forced it. Curve ends were placed by `metrics/calibration.py` anchor_curves from the labelled corpus with spans floored at three times the component's resampling sd and twice the human band width, and anchoring never saw the held-out slice -- `calibration.held_out` picks it by hashing the name, so separation is reported against negatives no curve was fitted to. Components asked for here that the analysis pass supplies -- decision_criticality, piece_utilisation, blunder_recoverability, instance_participation -- mean a corpus must be analysed before it can be scored under this version.

gradient_persistence.evidence: 2.6 / +0.21  central idea, noisy at four budgets

progress_irreversibility.evidence: 29.1 / band; -0.80 with blunder_recoverability, which came down for it

gates.reason: a searching player must beat a random one, or there is nothing to play
a game that mostly fails to finish is not a game
with no choices there is no play
a game that competent players almost always draw is not a contest
a game decided before either player has developed anything is not a game
doubling the thinking budget must be worth at least a few Elo, or skill does not exist here

a game where half of all contests are over in a handful of moves is decided by an opening trap, not by play; it correlates -0.89 with distinct_game_rate, so scoring it as well as gating it counted one measurement twice
